newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Saab's German sales rose 18 pct in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Saab's German sales rose 18 pct in Feb.

text.p: Swedish carmaker Saab Automobile said on Monday its sales in Germany rose 18 percent to 402 cars in February.
"During January and February the increase in the number of cars was 13 percent, to 806 cars," Saab Automobile spokesman Olof Wallen told Reuters.
The company's sales in Italy however plummeted 53 percent to 450 cars in January and February.
"We have had delivery problems, not least in the 900 Talladega model and the 9000 anniversary model, which are both in heavy demand," he said.
Wallen added that Italian distributors had also suffered a shortage of the popular cabriolet model but hoped to resolve the problem in March, April and May.
He said that advance orders had increased, indicating a sales recovery ahead.
Robert Hendry, president of Saab Automobile, identified the Germany and Italy as among the company's key markets, with the United States, Japan, Britain, Sweden, France and Australia.
Saab Automobile is jointly owned by investment company Investor AB of Sweden and U.S. automotive group General Motors. -- Henrik Alberius, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
